key_insight: Canopy unifies multimodal biological and experimental knowledge into a single heterogeneous graph foundation model that learns better strain-design representations than tabular or homogeneous graph baselines.
engineering_relevance: For metabolic engineering, this offers a scalable way to predict fermentation performance from relational biology instead of relying only on hand-crafted features or purely stoichiometric models.
method: Built a 6.9M-node, 13-node-type, 34-edge-type knowledge graph from 10 public and proprietary sources.
Encoded proteins, chemicals, and text with ESM-2, MoLFormer, and PubMedBERT before graph pretraining.
Trained an HGT model with SignNet positional encodings, Jumping Knowledge, virtual nodes, and four self-supervised losses.
evidence_signal: On fermentation titer prediction, frozen Canopy embeddings reached R² = 0.41 with a lightweight probe, beating the best tabular baseline at R² = 0.24.
watch_item: The model depends on heterogeneous data integration and several pretraining components, so performance may be sensitive to data quality, missing links, and graph construction choices.
paper_title: Canopy: A Heterograph Foundation Model for Metabolic Engineering
